'''Jordan Robert Farmar''' (born November 30, 1986) is an American-Israeli<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basketball.usbasket.com/player/Jordan-Farmar/NBA/Sacramento-Kings/65064|title = Jordan Farmar Player Profile, Sacramento Kings, News, Stats – USbasket}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=ג'ורדן פארמר: ''אני בכושר שיא. אולי אחזור לישראל'' - ערוץ הספורט |trans-title= |author= |work=Sport5.co.il - אתר ערוץ הספורט |date= October 9, 2020|access-date=21 December 2024 |url= https://www.sport5.co.il/articles.aspx?FolderID=403&docID=351298 |language=he}}
</ref> former professional [[basketball]] player who played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). In high school, he was named the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' High School Player of the Year in 2003–04. Playing [[college basketball]] for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]], he was the ''[[Rivals.com]]'' National Freshman of the Year in 2004–05. Farmar was selected 26th overall in the first round of the [[2006 NBA draft]] by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. With the Lakers, he won two [[List of NBA champions|NBA championships]] in 2009 and 2010.

==Early life==
Farmar was born in [[Los Angeles]]. His mother is named Melinda, known as "Mindy", and his father is Damon Farmar, a former [[minor league baseball]] outfielder who was a second round pick in both the 1981 January draft and the 1982 June draft secondary phase.<ref name="jewishjournal.com" /><ref name="ynet.co.il" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 29, 2002 |title=Jordan Farmar visits Gonzaga University |url=http://gonzaga.scout.com/2/72811.html |access-date=November 9, 2013 |website=Scout.com |archive-date=November 9, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131109203107/http://gonzaga.scout.com/2/72811.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Damon Farmar Minor League Statistics & History |url=https://www.baseball-reference.com/minors/player.cgi?id=farmar001dam |access-date=November 9, 2013 |publisher=Baseball-Reference.com}}</ref> His father is [[African-American]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/columns/story?page=arnovitzfarmar-081221|title = Lakers guard Jordan Farmar, the lone Jewish player in the NBA, hits the holidays at a crossroads of sorts|date = December 20, 2008}}</ref> His maternal grandfather, Dr. Howard Baker, attended UCLA and worked at the UCLA Medical Center as a neurologist.<ref name="UCLABio">{{Cite web |title=Player Bio: Jordan Farmar |url=http://www.uclabruins.com/ViewArticle.dbml?&DB_OEM_ID=30500&ATCLID=208185283 |access-date=November 9, 2013 |website=UCLABruins.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Anastasis |first=Louis |date=April 3, 2006 |title=UCLA's Farmar plays amid family worries |url=http://www.alligator.org/app/pt2/060403hoops4.php |access-date=November 9, 2013 |website=Alligator.org |archive-date=January 15, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160115093856/http://www.alligator.org/app/pt2/060403hoops4.php |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Alumni Notes |url=http://medicine.osu.edu/sitetool/sites/pdfs/medicinealumnipublic/AU_Fall_2005.pdf |access-date=November 9, 2013 |publisher=Medicine.OSU.edu}}</ref> Farmar has a half-sister, Shoshana Kolani.<ref name="jewishjournal.com">{{Cite web |last=Greenberg |first=Brad A. |date=April 23, 2009 |title=Jordan Farmar and the Jewish (Hoops) Future |url=http://www.jewishjournal.com/cover_story/article/jordan_farmar_and_the_jewish_hoops_future_20090422/ |access-date=November 9, 2013 |website=JewishJournal.com |publisher=Jewish Journal |archive-date=August 21, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100821070056/http://www.jewishjournal.com/cover_story/article/jordan_farmar_and_the_jewish_hoops_future_20090422/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Farmar's parents divorced when he was two years old, and he went to live with his mother. She soon met and married her current husband (Farmar's stepfather), [[Israel]]i Yehuda Kolani from [[Tel Aviv]].<ref name="jewishjournal.com" /><ref name="ynet.co.il">{{Cite news |last=Bogen |first=Amir |date=December 1, 2005 |title=UCLA's Jewish Jordan |newspaper= [[Ynetnews]] |url=http://www.ynetnews.com/articles/0,7340,L-3177805,00.html |access-date=January 27, 2011 |publisher=YNetNews.com}}</ref>

Farmar is [[Jewish]], as are his mother and stepfather.<ref name="ynet.co.il" /><ref name="JJ13773">{{Cite web |last=Davis |first=Carin |date=March 10, 2005 |title=Jewish Jordan Gives UCLA His Best Shot |url=http://www.jewishjournal.com/sports/article/jewish_jordan_gives_ucla_his_best_shot_20050311 |access-date=January 27, 2011 |website=JewishJournal.com |publisher=Jewish Journal}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Bogen |first=Amir |date=July 16, 2007 |title=Lakers star's Israeli link |url=http://www.ynetnews.com/articles/0,7340,L-3425115,00.html |access-date=January 27, 2011 |newspaper=Ynetnews}}</ref><ref name="Eager">{{Cite news |date=August 25, 2011 |title=Jordan Farmar eager to play in Israel |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/new-york/nba/story/_/id/6896047/new-jersey-nets-guard-jordan-farmar-lands-israel-eager-play |access-date=November 9, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=August 6, 2008 |title=Lakers guard Jordan Farmar conducts clinic in Israel |work=SeattleTimes |url=http://seattletimes.com/html/othersports/2008094405_digs06.html |url-status=dead |access-date=November 9, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006212241/http://seattletimes.com/html/othersports/2008094405_digs06.html |archive-date=October 6, 2014}}</ref> He attended [[Hebrew school]] and had his [[bar mitzvah]] at Temple Judea in [[Tarzana, California]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Jenkins |first=Lee |date=April 3, 2006 |title=The Bruins Let Farmar Do the Talking |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2006/04/03/sports/ncaabasketball/03farmar.html?_r=0 |access-date=April 3, 2006}}</ref>

Farmar started playing basketball at age 4.<ref name="jewishjournal.com" /> He credits his stepfather Yehuda Kolani with instilling discipline, mental strength, persistence, and a sense of obligation.<ref name="ynet.co.il" /><ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Aschburner |first=Steve |date=June 15, 2010 |title=This Father's Day is especially poignant for Celtics' Rivers |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2010/01/01/nba-finalsfathersday |access-date=December 5, 2015 |magazine=Sports Illustrated}}</ref> Farmar inherited his competitive drive from his father and mentor, Damon Farmar, who played football and baseball at University High and baseball in the minor leagues. The younger Farmar spent hours in his father's clubhouses, with his father's teammates, and watching his father play.<ref name=JJ13773/> Farmar's godfather is former major league baseball player [[Eric Davis (baseball)|Eric Davis]].<ref name="jordanfarmar.org" />

==High school career==
Farmar attended [[Portola Middle School (Tarzana)|Portola Middle School]] and Temple Judea<ref name="jewishjournal.com" /> in [[Tarzana, California|Tarzana]] and [[Birmingham High School]] in [[Van Nuys, California|Van Nuys]], before transferring his second year to [[Taft High School (Los Angeles)|Taft High School]] in [[Woodland Hills, Los Angeles|Woodland Hills]], a suburban community of the [[San Fernando Valley]] within Los Angeles.

At [[Taft High School (Los Angeles)|Taft High School]], Farmar scored a record 54 points in a single game.  As a junior, he averaged 28.5 points per game, 8.0 rebounds, 5.9 assists, and 4.5 steals.<ref name="jordanfarmar.org">{{Cite web |title=Jordan Farmar Biography – Los Angeles Lakers |url=http://www.jordanfarmar.org/jordanfarmarbio.php |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120222221314/http://www.jordanfarmar.org/jordanfarmarbio.php |archive-date=February 22, 2012 |access-date=May 30, 2010 |website=Jordanfarmar.org}}</ref> As a senior, he averaged 27.5 points and 6.5 assists, and led Taft to the school's first Los Angeles City title.  He had over 2,000 points in two seasons at Taft.<ref name="jordanfarmar.org" /> Farmar was named the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' Player of the Year, LA City Co-Player of the Year, and [[California Interscholastic Federation]] Los Angeles City Section High School Player of the Year. He earned ''[[USA Today]]'' Super 25 selection, second-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]], ''Slam Magazine'' Honorable Mention All-American, CalHi Sports All-State honors, and the [[Southern California]] Jewish Athlete of the Year.<ref name="UCLABio" /> He was a teammate with former [[New York Giants]] [[wide receiver]] [[Steve Smith (wide receiver, born 1985)|Steve Smith]].  Additionally, he was selected to play in the [[McDonald's]] High School All American game, where he scored 6 points and had 3 assists and 7 steals in 19 minutes of playing time.<ref name="UCLABio" />

==College career==
Considered one of the elite [[point guard]]s in the nation at UCLA, Farmar was named to the [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-10 First Team]] and the all Pac-10 Tournament team.  As a freshman in 2004–05, Farmar was the [[Rivals.com]] National Freshman of the Year, and [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Pac-10 Freshman of the Year]].  He led the team in assists (5.28 average) and free throw percentage (.801), and was # 2 in minutes (34.3) and points (13.2 points; # 1 among freshman guards), while topping all Pac-10 freshmen in scoring, assists, free throw percentage, and minutes played, as he was second in steals.<ref name="jordanfarmar.org" />

He was named [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-10]] First Team the next season. In the [[2006 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2006 NCAA Tournament]], Farmar led the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]] to the National Championship game against the [[Florida Gators]], which they lost by a score of 73–57.  Farmar led all scorers with 18 points, and finished with 2 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], 4 [[assist (basketball)|assists]], and 2 [[steal (basketball)|steals]]. Farmar made a notable steal and assist at the end of UCLA's [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship#Regional semifinals and finals|Sweet Sixteen]] matchup with the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs]], giving his team the lead for good after an impressive comeback effort.  On April 20, 2006, he declared for the [[NBA draft]].

==Professional career==

===Los Angeles Lakers (2006–2010)===
[[File:Jordan Farmar 2008.jpg|thumb|upright=0.6|left|Farmar in 2008]]
Farmar impressed NBA [[scout (sport)|scouts]] at the pre-draft combine with a {{convert|42|in|cm|adj=on|sigfig=2}} [[vertical leap]], the highest of any player there. Later, he was drafted by the Los Angeles Lakers with the 26th pick in the [[2006 NBA draft|NBA draft]], which was acquired along with [[Brian Grant]], [[Caron Butler]] and [[Lamar Odom]] in a trade that sent [[Shaquille O'Neal]] to the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2006 NBA Draft |url=http://nbahoopsonline.com/History/Leagues/NBA/drafts/2006.html |access-date=March 21, 2016 |website=NBAHoopsOnline.com}}</ref> On July 8, 2006, he made his debut at the [[Summer Pro League]], which was held at the [[Walter Pyramid]]. His final game totals were 17 points and 3 assists in 31 minutes of play.

For most of the [[2006–07 NBA season]], Farmar played backup to [[Smush Parker]]. On March 31, 2007, Farmar was assigned to the Lakers' [[NBA Development League|D-League]] team, the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 31, 2007 |title=Lakers Assign Farmar To D-Fenders |url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/lakers-assign-farmar-to-d-fenders/n-3444489 |access-date=March 21, 2016 |website=OurSportsCentral.com}}</ref> On April 1, Farmar scored 18 points in a 109–101 home loss against the [[Anaheim Arsenal]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 1, 2007 |title=Lakers Recall Farmar From D-Fenders |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/losangeles/farmar_recall_070401.html |access-date=January 27, 2011 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> Later on that afternoon, he was re-called by the Lakers to play against the visiting [[Sacramento Kings]]. Farmar added 4 points and 4 rebounds in 7:38 minutes playing time, helping the Lakers take a home victory, thereby making history by becoming the first player ever to participate in both a D-League and an NBA game on the same day.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 2, 2007 |title=Lakers Cruise to Victory Over Kings |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20070401/SACLAL/recap.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080503155116/http://www.nba.com/games/20070401/SACLAL/recap.html |archive-date=May 3, 2008 |access-date=January 27, 2011 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On April 15, against the [[Seattle SuperSonics]], Farmar got his first professional career start, replacing Parker in the starting lineup.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 15, 2007 |title=Kobe takes over in clutch as Lakers lock up playoff berth |url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=270415013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090107101652/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=270415013 |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 7, 2009 |access-date=March 21, 2016 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Along with two starts in the regular season, Farmar started all five playoff games at [[point guard]]. In those games against first round opponent the [[Phoenix Suns]], he averaged 6.4 ppg and 1.2 spg against [[Steve Nash]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jordan Farmar 2006–07 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/f/farmajo01/gamelog/2007/ |access-date=March 21, 2016 |website=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref>

With the departure of Smush Parker, [[Aaron McKie]], and [[Shammond Williams]], the Lakers lacked a point guard. Therefore, with the 19th selection in the [[2007 NBA draft]] the Los Angeles Lakers selected point guard [[Javaris Crittenton]], who was later traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. As a result, during the summer and fall of 2007 Farmar became a denizen of the team training facility, working on his shot from June through September. He knew his job was in jeopardy with a new point guard in town, and knew he had to work to keep his position within the organization. His hard work paid off, and he averaged 9.1 points, 2.2 rebounds, and 2.7 assists per game, in 20.6 minutes per game, as the backup to veteran point guard [[Derek Fisher]], who made his return to the Lakers. He played in all 82 games in the 2007–08 season, and shot 46.1% from the field, 3.9% up from the prior season, as well as 37.1% from three-point range, 4.3% up from the prior season. "I'm just trying to shorten [my shot], square my shoulders up and just knock it down", Farmar said.  "It's all [[hand–eye coordination]], and I believe in my ability."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bresnahan |first=Mike |date=December 1, 2007 |title=Farmar is not lacking for effort |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2007-dec-01-sp-lakerep1-story.html |access-date=March 21, 2016 |website=Los Angeles Times}}</ref> He had a career high of 24 points in a game against the Miami Heat.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 29, 2008 |title=Lakers Cool Off Heat for 10th Straight Win |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20080228/MIALAL/recap.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091003034147/http://www.nba.com/games/20080228/MIALAL/recap.html |archive-date=October 3, 2009 |access-date=January 27, 2011 |work=NBA.com}}</ref>

[[File:Jordan Farmar shooting vs Minnesota Timberwolves.jpg|thumb|upright=1.2|Farmar shooting against the Minnesota Timberwolves in 2010]]
On December 24, 2008, Farmar underwent surgery to repair a torn [[lateral meniscus]] in his left knee after suffering an injury in a game against the Miami Heat. He was expected to miss 8 weeks. Farmar was averaging 7.9 points and 2.4 assists before his injury. On January 25, 2009, Farmar returned to action nearly a month earlier than expected, recording 14 points and 2 assists against San Antonio.<ref>{{Cite news |date=January 25, 2009 |title=Lakers breeze to 99–85 victory over Spurs |work=NBA.com |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20090125/SASLAL/recap.html |access-date=March 21, 2016}}</ref>

On April 13, 2010, Farmar suffered a slight strain of his left hamstring, on the second-to-last game of the season. However, head coach [[Phil Jackson]] said Farmar would dress up for the season finale, to ensure that he would record a full 82-game season.<ref>{{cite news |last=McMenamin |first=Dave |date=April 13, 2010 | url=https://www.espn.com/los-angeles/nba/news/story?id=5084349|title=Farmar strains hamstring in home finale |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240812014334/https://www.espn.com/los-angeles/nba/news/story?id=5084349 |archive-date=August 12, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> He would recover in time for the playoffs, where he would help the team win a second consecutive championship.

=== New Jersey Nets (2010–2011) ===
After winning two championship rings with his hometown Los Angeles Lakers, Farmar agreed to a three-year, $12 million contract with the [[New Jersey Nets]] on July 14, 2010. A large factor in his decision was his feeling stifled playing behind the established Fisher with the Lakers.<ref name="mcmenamin_03012014">{{Cite news |last=McMenamin |first=Dave |date=March 1, 2014 |title=Jordan Farmar now comfortable in his role |work=ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/los-angeles/lakers/post/_/id/39039/jordan-farmar-now-comfortable-into-his-role |url-status=live |access-date=March 1, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140302004030/http://espn.go.com/blog/los-angeles/lakers/post/_/id/39039/jordan-farmar-now-comfortable-into-his-role |archive-date=March 2, 2014}}</ref> In 2010–11, he averaged 9.6 points per game on .467 field goal percentage.

===Maccabi Tel Aviv (2011)===
On August 3, 2011, Farmar signed a one-year contract with the [[Israeli Basketball Super League]] champion [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]], in the wake of the [[2011 NBA lockout]].<ref name="maccabiil">{{Cite news |date=August 2, 2011 |title=ג'ורדן פרמאר מצטרף למכבי אלקטרה ת"א |language=he |work=Maccabi.co.il |url=http://www.maccabi.co.il/News.asp?id=3068#sthash.ZHf5Mfl2.dpbs |access-date=August 4, 2011}}</ref> Farmar was very excited to go to [[Tel Aviv]], because his step-father is from the city, and he spent time there as a child.<ref name="Eager" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Sinai |first=Allon |date=August 4, 2011 |title=Mac TA brings Farmar aboard until NBA lockout is Settled |work=The Jerusalem Post |url=https://www.jpost.com/Sports/Article.aspx?id=232357 |access-date=August 4, 2011}}</ref><ref name="autogenerated1" />

Because Farmar is Jewish, he is eligible to apply for [[Israeli citizenship]], and he has expressed an interest in doing so.<ref name="autogenerated1" /><ref name="nytimes1" /> That way he would be considered an Israeli player, and thereby avoid being counted against the Israeli league's limit of four non-Israeli players per team.<ref name="nytimes1" /> He would also be eligible to play for the [[Israel national basketball team]] in the [[Basketball at the Summer Olympics|Olympics]] and other international competitions.<ref name="autogenerated1" />
[[File:Jordan Farmar - Maccabi.jpg|thumb|upright=0.8|Farmar with Maccabi Tel Aviv in 2011]]
Farmar began playing for the team when its season began on October 1, 2011.<ref name="autogenerated1">{{Cite news |last=Stephenson |first=Colin |date=August 3, 2011 |title=Nets' Jordan Farmar agrees to deal with Maccabi Tel Aviv |work=NJ.com |url=http://www.nj.com/nets/index.ssf/2011/08/nets_jordan_farmar_agrees_to_d.html |access-date=August 4, 2011}}</ref><ref name="nytimes1">{{Cite news 27, 2011 |title=NBA recruit Farmar focuses on leading Mac TA to glory |work=The Jerusalem Post |url=https://www.jpost.com/Sports/Article.aspx?id=239801 |access-date=October 2, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{Cite |url=https://www.jpost.com/Sports/Yellow-and-blue-opens-Adriatic-League-campaign-in-style |access-date=October 2, 2011}}</ref> His teammates included former [[All-American]] [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] guard [[Jon Scheyer]], who joined the team in June.<ref>{{Cite news |date=August 3, 2011 |title=Jordan Farmar signs with Tel Aviv |publisher=ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/new-york/nba/story/_/id/6830970/new-jersey-nets-guard-jordan-farmar-signs-israeli-champions |access-date=August 4, 2011}}</ref> In the first week of November 2011, he won |url=https://www.haaretz.com/print-edition/sports/farmer-s-last-game-with-maccabi-tel-aviv-sees-sorry-end-against-partizan-belgrade-1.399104 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111202185126/http://www.haaretz.com/print-edition/sports/farmer-s-last-game-with-maccabi-tel-aviv-sees-sorry-end-against-partizan-belgrade-1.399104 |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 2, 2011 |access-date=October 17, 2012 |website=Haaretz}}</ref> He averaged 14.1 points in seven [[EuroLeague]] games.<ref name="Eurostats">{{Cite web |title=FARMAR, Jordan – Euroleague stats |url=http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=003423#!careerstats |access-date=March 21, 2016 |website=Euroleague.net}}</ref>

=== Return to the Nets (2011–2012) ===
Farmar returned to the [[Brooklyn Nets|New Jersey Nets]] after the NBA lockout ended.

On March 7, 2012, Farmar hit an open game-winning 3-point shot against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], leaving the clock with 0.2 seconds left. The final score was 101–100.<ref>{{Cite news |date=March 7, 2012 |title=Notebook: Nets 101, Clippers 100 |work=NBA.com |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20120307/LACNJN/gameinfo.html |access-date=March 21, 2016}}</ref> In 2011–12, he averaged 10.4 points per game and 5.0 assists per game, as he played 24.6 minutes per game.

On July 11, 2012, Farmar, [[Anthony Morrow]], [[Jordan Williams (basketball, born 1990)|Jordan Williams]], [[Johan Petro]], [[DeShawn Stevenson]], and a 2013 first round draft pick were traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] for [[Joe Johnson (basketball)|Joe Johnson]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 11, 2012 |title=TWO MAJOR TRANSACTIONS SIGNIFICANTLY RESHAPE HAWKS FUTURE |url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/two-major-transactions-significantly-reshape-hawks-future |access-date=July 11, 2012 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> Five days later, he was waived by the Hawks.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 16, 2012 |title=ATLANTA HAWKS REQUEST WAIVERS ON JORDAN FARMAR |url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-request-waivers-jordan-farmar |access-date=July 16, 2012 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Anadolu Efes (2012–2013)===
On July 12, 2012, Farmar signed a three-year $15 million contract, with opt-outs after each season,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Woelfel |first=Gery |date=June 13, 2013 |title=BUCKS BLOG: Milwaukee has its eye on Caldwell-Pope |url=http://journaltimes.com/sports/basketball/bucks-blog-milwaukee-has-its-eye-on-caldwell-pope/article_f0f56ce2-d4ac-11e2-a45f-001a4bcf887a.html |access-date=November 9, 2013 |website=JournalTimes.com |publisher=Journal Times}}</ref> with the [[Turkish Basketball Super League|Turkish League]] team [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 12, 2012 |title=Anadolu Efes Istanbul officially signs Jordan Farmar |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/93457/anadolu-efes-istanbul-officially-signs-jordan-farmar.html |access-date=October 17, 2012 |website=Sportando.com}}</ref> He averaged 13.8 points in 29 EuroLeague games.<ref name="Eurostats" />

===Return to the Lakers (2013–2014)===
On July 17, 2013, Farmar returned to the Lakers, signing for the 2013–14 season.<ref>{{Cite news |date=July 17, 2013 |title=Lakers Sign Jordan Farmar |work=NBA.com |url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/130717_jordan_farmar |access-date=November 9, 2013}}</ref> On December 1, Farmar tore his left [[hamstring]] and was expected to miss a month of action. He only played 56 seconds before leaving the game. On February 28, 2014, he scored a career-high 30 points in a 126–122 win over Sacramento. He was a career-high 8-for-10 on 3-pointers in the game, and the Lakers set a franchise record for most threes made in a regulation game, shooting 19-for-27.<ref name=mcmenamin_03012014/> In 2013–14, he averaged 10.1 points per game, 4.9 assists per game, and 2.5 rebounds per game.

===Los Angeles Clippers (2014–2015)===
On July 9, 2014, Farmar signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=July 9, 2014 |title=CLIPPERS SIGN FARMAR AND HAWES |work=NBA.com |url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/clippers-sign-farmar-and-hawes |access-date=July 9, 2014}}</ref> The team signed him to replace former UCLA teammate [[Darren Collison]], who left the Clippers as a free agent.<ref name="markazi_01282015">{{Cite news |last=Markazi |first=Arash |date=January 28, 2015 |title=Austin Rivers hitting his stride for Clippers |work=ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/los-angeles/clippers/post/_/id/7309/austin-rivers-hitting-his-stride-for-clippers |url-status=live |access-date=February 7, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150207100304/http://espn.go.com/blog/los-angeles/clippers/post/_/id/7309/austin-rivers-hitting-his-stride-for-clippers |archive-date=February 7, 2015}}</ref> Farmar never quite fit in with the team, and was waived on January 16, 2015, after agreeing to a buyout. He had complained of an inconsistent role and playing time on the team, while coaches were unhappy with his performance.<ref name=markazi_01282015/><ref name=markazi_01162015/> In 36 games, he averaged 4.6 points, 1.9 assists and 1.2 rebounds.<ref name="markazi_01162015">{{Cite news |last=Markazi |first=Arash |date=January 16, 2015 |title=Clippers waive Jordan Farmar |work=ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/los-angeles/nba/story/_/id/12180149/los-angeles-clippers-waive-jordan-farmar |url-status=live |access-date=January 16, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150117121815/http://espn.go.com/los-angeles/nba/story/_/id/12180149/los-angeles-clippers-waive-jordan-farmar |archive-date=January 17, 2015}}</ref>

===Darüşşafaka (2015)===
On February 7, 2015, Farmar signed with [[Darüşşafaka Basketbol|Darüşşafaka]] of Turkey for the rest of the [[2014–15 Turkish Basketball League]] season.<ref>{{Cite news |date=February 7, 2015 |title=Darussafaka Dogus lands Jordan Farmar |work=Sportando.com |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/151460/darussafaka-dogus-lands-jordan-farmar.html |access-date=February 7, 2015}}</ref> He averaged 14.9 points in 14 Turkish national league games.<ref name="Eurostats" />

===Return to Maccabi Tel Aviv (2015–2016)===

On July 6, 2015, he returned to Maccabi Tel Aviv, signing a contract for the 2015–16 season.<ref>{{Cite news |date=July 6, 2015 |title=Jordan Farmar Returns to Maccabi |work=maccabi.co.il |url=http://maccabi.co.il/News.asp?id=4953&lang=en#sthash.ovjirmWD.dpbs |access-date=July 6, 2015}}</ref> On January 10, 2016, he parted ways with Maccabi.<ref>{{Cite news |date=January 10, 2016 |title=Farmar and Maccabi Part Ways |work=maccabi.co.il |url=http://maccabi.co.il/News.asp?id=5218&lang=en#sthash.d7TH4Oxw.dpbs |access-date=January 10, 2016}}</ref> He averaged 8.9 points, 2.4 rebounds, and 2.8 assists in eight [[EuroLeague]] games.<ref name="Eurostats" />

===Memphis Grizzlies (2016)===
On March 21, 2016, Farmar signed a 10-day contract with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=March 21, 2016 |title=Grizzlies sign Jordan Farmar to 10-day contract |work=NBA.com |url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/jordan-farmar-160321 |access-date=March 21, 2016}}</ref> That night, he made his debut for the Grizzlies in a 103–97 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]], recording 12 points, three rebounds, one assist, and one steal in 23 minutes.<ref>{{Cite news |date=March 22, 2016 |title=Stephenson leads Grizzlies past Suns, 103–97 |work=NBA.com |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160321/MEMPHX/gameinfo.html |access-date=March 22, 2016}}</ref> On March 31, he signed with the Grizzlies for the rest of the season.<ref>{{Cite news |date=March 31, 2016 |title=Grizzlies sign Jordan Farmar for the remainder of the 2015–16 Season |work=NBA.com |url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/farmar-signed-for-season-160331 |access-date=March 31, 2016}}</ref> Then, on the same day, Farmar scored a season-high 14 points and dished out 5 assists in a losing effort against the Denver Nuggets.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 31, 2016 |title=Barton helps Nuggets beat Grizzlies 109–105 |url=http://www.espn.com.au/nba/recap?gameId=400829001 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180901182522/http://www.espn.com.au/nba/recap?gameId=400829001 |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 1, 2018 |access-date=September 1, 2018 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> On April 5, Farmar, scored a new season-high with 15 points in a 108–92 victory over the visiting Chicago Bulls. He also grabbed 2 rebounds and dished out 4 assists.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 5, 2016 |title=Randolph's double-double leads Grizzlies past Bulls, 108–92 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400829045 |access-date=September 1, 2018 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

=== Sacramento Kings (2016) ===
On September 14, 2016, Farmar signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 14, 2016 |title=Kings Sign Jordan Farmar |url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-jordan-farmar |access-date=September 14, 2016 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He was waived by the Kings on October 24,<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 24, 2016 |title=Kings Waive Two |url=http://www.nba.com/kings/new/kings-waive-two |access-date=October 24, 2016 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> and later re-signed on November 2.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 2, 2016 |title=Kings Sign Jordan Farmar |url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-farmar |access-date=November 2, 2016 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On November 7, he was waived by the Kings after appearing in two games.<ref>{{Cite news |date=November 7, 2016 |title=Kings Waive Jordan Farmar |work=NBA.com |url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-waive-farmar |access-date=November 7, 2016}}</ref>

==Accolades==
In 2010 he was inducted into the [[Southern California Jewish Sports Hall of Fame]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Southern California Jewish Sports Hall of Fame Home |url=https://scjewishsportshof.com/farmar.html}}</ref>

==Personal life==
On July 29, 2012, Farmar married soccer player [[Jill Oakes]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 18, 2013 |title=Jill Oakes & Jordan Farmar |url=http://modernluxury.com/brides-california/story/jill-oakes-jordan-farmar |access-date=November 9, 2013 |publisher=ModernLuxury.com}}</ref>

Farmar has a tattoo on his left arm of him with his arm around his little half-sister, while the words "just the two of us" surround them. He also has a tattoo across his back that reads "Farmar." He is a [[Barack Obama]] supporter, and attended a fundraiser for Obama in [[Orange County, California]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Overly |first=Jeff |date=July 13, 2008 |title=Barack Obama raises more than $1 million in O.C. |work=OCRegister.com |publisher=[[Orange County Register]] |url=http://www.ocregister.com/articles/obama-county-orange-2092770-democratic-going |access-date=July 14, 2008 |archive-date=July 14, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080714133420/http://www.ocregister.com/articles/obama-county-orange-2092770-democratic-going |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2009, Farmar played himself in the television series ''[[Numbers (TV series)|Numb3rs]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Medina |first=Mark |date=March 13, 2009 |title='Numb3rs' lures two Lakers to Caltech |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2009-mar-13-et-lakers13-story.html |access-date=March 21, 2016 |website=Los Angeles Times}}</ref>

==Philanthropy==
In one week in August 2008, he led a basketball camp for Israeli and [[Palestinian people|Palestinian]] children, having them play together on the same team.<ref name="jewishjournal.com" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hoffman |first=Gil |date=August 7, 2008 |title=Laker Jordan Farmar shoots for Middle East coexistence |url=http://www.interfaithfamily.com/arts_and_entertainment/popular_culture/Laker_Jordan_Farmar_shoots_for_Middle_East_coexistence.shtml |access-date=May 30, 2010 |publisher=InterfaithFamily.com |archive-date=July 13, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110713050135/http://www.interfaithfamily.com/arts_and_entertainment/popular_culture/Laker_Jordan_Farmar_shoots_for_Middle_East_coexistence.shtml |url-status=dead }}</ref> He also started Hoop Farm, a children's basketball camp at [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] which he leads that promotes [[eco-friendly]] behavior.<ref name="jewishjournal.com" />

He joined the [[Chabad]] [[Telethon]] in September 2008, shooting free-throws in order to raise funds.  Rabbi Chaim Cunin, executive producer of the telethon and CEO of Chabad of California, said: "Jordan is a real [[mensch]]. He raised $66,600 in 90 seconds.  He made 37 free throws in 90 seconds."<ref name="jewishjournal.com" />

In 2009, during the summer he was the host of the first annual Jordan Farmar Celebrity Golf Classic, which was held at [[Sherwood Country Club]] in [[Thousand Oaks]].  The money that was raised was contributed to the Jordan Farmar Foundation, which his mother runs and which is focused on assisting at-risk youths and children who are taking [[cancer treatment]] at [[Ronald Reagan UCLA Medical Center#UCLA Mattel Children's Hospital|Mattel Children's Hospital UCLA]].<ref name="jewishjournal.com" />
